corrections.source_says: The methods explicitly report random assignment of the two intact classes during ordinary coursework. Under the codebook, this is a reported field_rct with class-level assignment, not quasi_people, which requires non-random assignment. Retain the authors' conflicting description of the study as quasi-experimental and the limitation of one class per arm in the design notes.
corrections.quote: The two selected classes were then randomly assigned to a control group (33 students) and an experimental group (31 students) to reduce the likelihood of systematic baseline differences between the groups.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 12, Research design: Participants and Experimental design; creativity-codebook.md section 4 and form-spec.md design_class field note

corrections.source_says: Set to met for the reported random assignment of classes to an intervention containing generative-AI assistance versus traditional PBL. Class-level rather than individual assignment, the authors' quasi-experimental label, and the bundled VR intervention should be documented, but do not negate the explicit random-assignment statement. This does not change core exclusion because criterion 3 fails.
corrections.quote: The two selected classes were then randomly assigned to a control group (33 students) and an experimental group (31 students) to reduce the likelihood of systematic baseline differences between the groups.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 12, Participants; pp. 13-14, Experimental design and Experimental environment; creativity-codebook.md sections 3 and 10

corrections.form_value: Criterion 3 fails: every creativity outcome is a self-report Likert questionnaire, and the paper says it relies exclusively on self-report questionnaires (p. 23). No output was rated, so the study is listed in the screening report and omitted from the dataset. Criterion 1 is unclear: the text says two intact classes were randomly assigned (p. 12), one class per arm, so individuals were not randomized, the paper itself calls the design quasi-experimental, and the treatment bundles VR immersion with the LLM assistant. Criterion 2 is met with 63 students analyzed (31 vs 32).
corrections.source_says: Replace the uncertainty about assignment with the explicit reported random assignment of two intact classes, one per arm. Retain core = no and context_class = none because the analyzed creativity outcomes are exclusively self-reports, with no reported research outcome scored on student products; criterion 2 is met by 63 analyzed students (31 AI-IVE-PBL, 32 T-PBL). The VR and LLM components are bundled, so the contrast does not isolate the LLM contribution.
corrections.quote: The research initially relies exclusively on self-report questionnaires for data collection, a method susceptible to subjective bias.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 12, Participants; pp. 13-14, intervention descriptions; pp. 18-19, Tables 1-2; p. 23, Limitations and future research

corrections.form_value: Two intact first-year classes of an Interior Art Design major at a vocational college in Fuzhou, China, took a 12-week Public Space Interior Design course with the same instructor. One class used project-based learning in an AI-enabled immersive virtual environment (PICO 4 VR headsets, SketchUp, and an AI teaching assistant built on the iFLYTEK Xinghuo large model); the other used traditional project-based learning with drawing tablets and AutoCAD. The outcomes are self-report Likert questionnaires on design creativity (pretest and posttest), learning engagement, and learning experience; no student output was rated.
corrections.source_says: Narrow the final claim to: no reported research outcome was scored on student products. The classroom workflow does describe a design/presentation rubric and self-, peer-, and teacher evaluations of proposals. Those pedagogical evaluations are not reported as study outcome data; the analyzed creativity measures remain self-report questionnaires.
corrections.quote: Teachers provide a design and presentation rubric outlining criteria for aesthetics, layout, functionality, and collaboration. After reviewing all proposals, students conduct self-, peer-, and teacher evaluations, with results shared online for transparency.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 11, Course implementation, (5) Refinement; p. 15, Design creativity survey; pp. 23-24, Limitations and future research

confirmed: The source is the 30-page journal article by Shuaizhen Jin, Zheng Zhong, Xu Cao, and Wenzhuo Zhang, headed Research and Practice in Technology Enhanced Learning (2027) 22:29 with copyright 2026; p. 27 states Published online: 1 January 2027 (Online First: 8 September 2026). The complete markdown, including the appendices and references, was read, and the recorded numbers were checked against PDF text (PDF pp. 1, 27; document page count).

The assigned classes contained 31 experimental and 33 control students; these are people within two randomized classes, not 64 independent assignment units (PDF p. 12, Participants; p. 17, Data collection and analysis).

The paper reports 64 questionnaires collected and 63 valid responses retained, then explicitly identifies 63 participants; Tables 1-2 show 31 AI-IVE-PBL and 32 T-PBL analyzed. The counts support the form's inference that the invalid response was from the control class; the analyzed total meets the 50-person threshold (PDF pp. 17-19).
The analyzed sample comprises 29 males and 34 females, with 96.83% aged 19-20 years (PDF p. 18, Analysis of students' situation and Table 1).
The course lasted 12 weeks with one instructor for both groups; its projects were Aviation Exhibition Hall Design, Memorial Hall Design, and Construction Drawing Deepening Design (PDF pp. 9, 12).

The intervention bundled PICO 4 VR devices, SketchUp, and an AI teaching assistant using the iFLYTEK Xinghuo model API and its language-generation capabilities; the control used drawing tablets, AutoCAD, and conventional teaching resources (PDF pp. 13-14).

Each design-creativity subscale has four self-report items on a 5-point Likert scale. The three example items in the form match the instrument text, and ANCOVA uses pretest creativity as a covariate (PDF p. 15, Design creativity survey; pp. 18-19, RQ1; p. 25, Appendix 1).
Creative ability: AI-IVE-PBL M = 4.00, SD = 0.44, n = 31; T-PBL M = 3.73, SD = 0.61, n = 32; F(1, 60) = 7.465, p = .008, partial eta squared = .111 (PDF p. 19, Table 2 and RQ1 text).
Design ability: AI-IVE-PBL M = 3.98, SD = 0.51, n = 31; T-PBL M = 3.62, SD = 0.62, n = 32; F(1, 60) = 9.630, p = .003, partial eta squared = .138 (PDF p. 19, Table 2 and RQ1 text).
Innovative thinking: AI-IVE-PBL M = 4.05, SD = 0.53, n = 31; T-PBL M = 3.85, SD = 0.65, n = 32; F(1, 60) = 2.570, p = .114, partial eta squared = .041 (PDF p. 19, Table 2 and RQ1 text).
All numbers and directions in the one_line_finding match Table 2: self-rated creative ability and design ability differ significantly, while innovative thinking does not (PDF p. 19).

No qualifying randomized study with creativity or diversity scored on participant output is reported: the study explicitly relies exclusively on self-report questionnaires, and expert ratings of design artifacts are proposed for future studies. Accordingly has_randomized_people_study = false under this check's output-scoring requirement, core = no, criterion 3 = not_met, and context_class = none remain appropriate (PDF pp. 15, 17, 23-25).

Appendices 1-3 are included in the article and contain questionnaire items, not additional output-rated outcomes or effect estimates; no separate supplement is identified. This is an empirical intervention study, not a synthesis, so the synthesis fields properly remain empty (PDF pp. 12-20, 25-26).

The PDF names academic author affiliations and National Natural Science Foundation of China funding, declares no competing interests, and makes data available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request; it supplies no public data or code URL (PDF pp. 26-27).
summary: The participant counts and all three Table 2 results are correct, and no qualifying randomized study with creativity or diversity scored on output is reported. Corrections are needed to recognize the stated class randomization and to distinguish classroom design evaluations from the study's self-report outcomes.
